app.subtitle: fine-tuning of laptop CPU power plans
editor.restoreTip: Fill in the plan's original values (from the backup). Applied with “Save”.
editor.hint: Changes accumulate and are applied with “Save”. The marker on a slider is the original value.
editor.gHelper: G-Helper / Armoury switch plans together with their modes — this app never switches plans by itself.
msg.notActive: The plan is not active — use “Make active” to switch to it.
msg.restored: Original values filled in. “Save” to apply.

msg.copied: Value copied to the other column.
confirm.title: You have unsaved changes
ctl.eppP.name: P-core EPP
ctl.eppP.help: The main knob. A hint to the CPU: 0 = maximum speed, 100 = maximum efficiency. Higher → lower clocks, fewer watts and degrees, slower response. Typically 30–65 plugged in, 50–85 on battery. → cooler
ctl.eppE.name: E-core EPP
ctl.eppE.help: The same for the efficiency cores where background work lives. Can be kept higher than for P-cores: cooler background without losing responsiveness. → cooler
ctl.boost.name: Turbo boost
ctl.boost.help: Permission to run above base clock. “Disabled” is the strongest way to cut heat (−10–20 °C), but the CPU gets noticeably slower. “Efficient” boosts less often. → cooler
ctl.maxstate.name: Max performance
ctl.maxstate.help: Performance ceiling. 100 % = no limit. Lower means much lower clocks and heat; on many CPUs 99 % disables turbo boost. ← cooler
ctl.freqP.name: P-core frequency limit
ctl.freqP.help: Hard P-core clock cap, 0 = no limit. The last 500–1000 MHz add little speed but a lot of heat — a good way to cool the laptop down. ← cooler
ctl.freqE.name: E-core frequency limit
ctl.freqE.help: E-core clock cap, 0 = no limit. Affects background work more than games. ← cooler
ctl.minstate.name: Min performance
ctl.minstate.help: Performance floor. Keep it at 5 %: higher values stop the CPU from cooling down at idle. ← cooler
ctl.park.name: Min active cores
ctl.park.help: How many cores to keep awake at all times. 100 % = core parking off: smoother response, slightly more watts at idle. A low value is better on battery. ← more efficient
ctl.sched.name: Where to place tasks
ctl.sched.help: How Windows splits threads between P- and E-cores. “Auto” lets Thread Director decide. “E first” is cooler and quieter; heavy work still moves to P-cores. “E only” is much slower. → cooler
ctl.contain.name: Background on E-cores
ctl.contain.help: Windows 11 containment zones: light load is held on E-cores and does not wake P-cores. Hydroc uses proven 50/60 % thresholds. One of the main remedies for heat at idle.
ctl.latency.name: Response to input
ctl.latency.help: When you click or open a window, Windows briefly raises the clock. “Efficient” (as in Hydroc) removes these spikes: less heat and fewer watts, the UI may feel slightly less snappy.
ctl.hwp.name: Who controls frequency
ctl.hwp.help: HWP — the CPU picks its clock every millisecond taking EPP into account. “CPU” is recommended. “Windows” is the legacy way: slower to react, EPP works worse.
ctl.aspm.name: PCIe power saving
ctl.aspm.help: PCIe link sleep (SSD, Wi-Fi, GPU). Saves 1–3 W at idle. If you see stutters or Wi-Fi drops, set it back to “Off”. → more efficient
ctl.cooling.name: Cooling policy
ctl.cooling.help: Active — fans first, then lower clocks. Passive — lower clocks first: quieter but slower under load. On ASUS the fan curves are set by G-Helper/Armoury.
preset.quiet.name: Quiet and cool
preset.quiet.desc: minimum noise and heat, background on E-cores
preset.hydroc.name: Balance (Hydroc)
preset.hydroc.desc: Hydroc logic: EPP 64/80, background on E, no spikes
preset.hydrocSoft.name: Hydroc softer
preset.hydrocSoft.desc: Hydroc with mid EPP: more speed, slightly warmer
preset.perf.name: Performance
preset.perf.desc: games and heavy work, fast response
preset.battery.name: Max battery
preset.battery.desc: changes “on battery” only: boost off, EPP 90/95
preset.note: A preset only fills in values — you save them. Presets never touch frequency limits.
eco.title: Background apps on E-cores
eco.noHybrid: All cores are the same type — “E-cores only” is unavailable
eco.explain: Eco — Windows treats the app as background work (EcoQoS, like “Efficiency mode” in Task Manager): it runs on E-cores at low clocks and does not wake P-cores. E-cores only — additionally pins it to the efficiency cores: coolest, but the app is slower. Don't use it for games or apps you actively work in.
eco.note: A mode lasts while the app is running. CPU Balancer in the tray re-applies it every time the app starts and re-checks every 30 s.
eco.msg.denied: Some processes are protected by the system — access denied.
eco.msg.autostart: To keep modes working after a reboot, enable “Start at sign-in” in Settings.
settings.autostartDesc: A Task Scheduler task with administrator rights: the app starts in the tray without a UAC prompt and applies background app modes right away.
settings.v1: Found the v1 task “CPU Balancer - фон на E-ядрах” (PowerShell watcher). v2 does the same from inside the app — replace it?
settings.updatesDesc: Notification only: a request to GitHub Releases, nothing is downloaded automatically.
settings.dataDirDesc: Plan backups, background app list, settings. Next to the exe (portable).
settings.tray: Closing the window minimizes the app to the tray. Exit from the tray icon menu.
